purpose: Repeatable PostgreSQL schema delivery for the program-owned canonical model

migration_naming.collision_policy: CI requires unique version identifiers and valid names before merge.
migration_naming.repeatable_scope: Views, functions, and other replaceable definitions whose complete desired form is safe to reapply.
migration_naming.immutability: Applied versioned migration bytes remain stable; corrections arrive through a later timestamped migration.

expand: add indexes with lock-aware PostgreSQL techniques
deploy code that can operate across the transition
transition: compare canonical reads and representative distributions
contract: move readers and writers to the canonical structure
remove compatibility structures in a later release

transactional_outbox.scope: Cross-service domain events that must commit with aggregate changes.
application_responsibility: write aggregate state and one immutable outbox record in the same transaction
publish stable event identifiers and versioned payload schemas
measure event age and consumer lag
connector_responsibility: route outbox records to the configured broker topic
preserve the event key and declared headers

vendor_lifecycle.boundary: Sapio, Benchling, LabKey, and other products retain their vendor-supported upgrade and configuration mechanisms.

checks: clean installation reaches the expected schema
supported predecessor upgrade preserves representative data
late timestamped migrations apply with outOfOrder enabled
Flyway validate reports valid checksums and naming
Flyway info exposes pending, applied, and out-of-order state
transactional failure preserves the predecessor state
clean install and upgraded catalog projections converge
application integration tests pass against the migrated schema

metadata.next_review_trigger: A supported database major, Flyway release, broker topology, or vendor lifecycle changes.
